newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB says SIC can be adapted to clear euros.
newsitem.headline: SNB says SIC can be adapted to clear euros.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) council member Bruno Gehrig said it would cost relatively little to adapt the Swiss Interbank Clearing System (SIC) so it could clear euros as well as Swiss francs.

Gehrig said SIC essentially fulfills all the European Union's (EU) requirements for payment systems to be connected with EU's planned Trans-European Automated Real-Time Gross Settlement Express Transfer System (TARGET).
"With relatively little expense SIC could be adjusted so it not only settles Swiss francs, but also euros," Gehrig said.

If an expanded SIC were connected with TARGET, then Swiss banks could settle euro transactions between each other and with EU banks considerably more efficiently than via the normal ties to correspondent banks, Gehrig said.

"Considering the safety and efficiency of the euro payment traffic, we prefer a solution in which transactions are directly settled and not indirectly -- that is via correspondent banks," Gehrig said.

Swiss banks expect a considerable part of their future payments volume to be in euro and are therefore looking for ways to settle this that in more efficient way than through correspondent banks in countries that will participate in a single European currency.
Gehrig noted that the EU still had not decided on how the payment systems in non-EU countries should be linked to TARGET.

The SNB is an observer in an ad-hoc working group set up by banks to study the issue of how euro transactions can be settled in Switzerland and the central bank is also in close touch with the European Monetary Institute (EMI).
